q: Does the two-lineage split of S. Bovismorbificans survive a proper bootstrapped core-genome maximum-likelihood phylogeny, and is the ST150 branch statistically well-supported rather than being an artifact of mash distance + average-linkage clustering with n=2 for that lineage?
basis: Our replication recovered the paper's two-polyphyletic-cluster topology using mash all-vs-all distances + average-linkage hierarchical clustering at a 2-cluster cut, which is a proxy for phylogeny and provides no branch-support values. The ST150 'separate lineage' rests on only 2 genomes in our set; the paper's own support comes from a bespoke 2690-locus core-genome schema and DNA-tiling-array evidence that we did not rebuild. A single well-supported ML tree with bootstraps would decide whether the split is a real deep divergence or a clustering geometry choice.
next_steps: Take the 82 assemblies + 150 complete reference Salmonella genomes; call core-genome SNPs against S. Typhimurium LT2 (or a closer Bovismorbificans reference) with snippy or Parsnp; construct a core-SNP alignment; build a RAxML-NG or IQ-TREE ML tree with GTR+GAMMA and >=1000 ultra-fast bootstraps; also run a parsimony tree and a Bayesian tree (MrBayes/BEAST2) as cross-checks; measure the bootstrap/posterior on the internal branch separating ST150 from the {142,377,1499,2640} backbone; sweep additional ST150 isolates from Enterobase to raise n above 2 before drawing lineage conclusions.

q: What is the actual within-backbone phylogenetic structure of the ST142/377/1499/2640 cluster, and are ST377 (US hummus-outbreak) and ST1499 truly two distinct sub-lineages inside the backbone or a single continuum with STs assigned by 7-gene MLST noise?
basis: The paper groups {2640,142,1499,377} together as one polyphyletic lineage but does not resolve internal structure in a way we could test. Our 2-cluster mash cut collapses all four backbone STs into one bin (n=80); we never asked what a 4- or 5-cluster cut would look like. Given ST377 is tied to the US hummus outbreaks and ST1499 has a distinct clinical/food mix in our metadata, they may represent independent introductions that a coarse cut obscures.
next_steps: Recluster the 80 backbone genomes at increasing k (2,3,4,5,6) using both mash distance and a proper core-SNP tree; compute cluster stability metrics (silhouette width, gap statistic, prediction strength) to pick the natural k; overlay isolation source, geography, and outbreak metadata on the resulting sub-clusters; test whether ST377's hummus-outbreak genomes form a tight monophyletic sub-clade with recent MRCA (using BEAST tip-dating on collection dates); check whether ST1499 shares ancestry preferentially with ST142 or ST377.

q: Is the pVirBov virulence plasmid a single conserved replicon across the 56/82 spvD-positive genomes, or does the spv-carrying plasmid show pan-plasmid variability (rearrangements, cargo swaps, loss of subsets of spvABCDR) that would matter clinically?
basis: The paper highlights pVirBov and the spv virulence-plasmid locus as biologically important. We reproduced spvD presence in 56/82 assemblies at the feature-class level with AMRFinderPlus, but we never assembled the plasmid, did not identify its replicon type, did not check whether the full spvRABCD operon is intact or truncated, and did not compare plasmid backbones between clinical and food isolates. A conserved-vs-mosaic pVirBov distinction is directly downstream of the paper's own discussion.
next_steps: For each spvD+ isolate, run mob-suite (mob_recon/mob_typer) to reconstruct plasmid contigs and assign replicon types; extract the plasmid FASTA sets and cluster them with mash + Mashtree, or align with progressive Mauve, to detect rearrangements; check completeness of the spvRABCD operon per plasmid with BLAST against a pVirBov reference; correlate plasmid variants with source (clinical/food) and geography; where short-read assemblies leave the plasmid fragmented, request or generate long-read (ONT) reassemblies for a subset to resolve the true plasmid architecture.

q: How does Bovismorbificans's population structure and AMR carriage look when the sampling is extended beyond the paper's Switzerland/USA/Canada set to a globally representative pull from Enterobase/GenomeTrakr, and does the two-lineage claim generalize outside this geographic window?
basis: The paper's 81 newly-sequenced isolates are Swiss (majority) + a small US/Canada tail; we recovered essentially the same skew (75 CH / 5 CA / 2 US). Whether {2640,142,1499,377} vs ST150 is a global partition or a partition specific to European/North American clinical surveillance is not established. There is also a possibility that additional STs (e.g. rare ones) exist in African, Asian, or Latin American isolates and would break the clean two-cluster picture.
next_steps: Query Enterobase's Salmonella database for all serovar Bovismorbificans genomes with country and year metadata; add all NCBI Pathogen Detection SNP-cluster hits assigned to Bovismorbificans; deduplicate against the paper's 82; rebuild the mash and ML trees at n=few-hundred to few-thousand; check whether the ST150 branch is truly separate at global scale or becomes one of many minor branches; test whether AMR carriage patterns (esp. ESBL blaCTX-M, plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance) show geographic gradients not visible in the paper's Swiss-dominated set.

q: Can the paper's bespoke 2690-locus core-genome schema and the k-mer-binning-of-260+-strains method be re-implemented from open-source components and shown to give equivalent lineage assignments to what we recovered by the mash proxy - i.e., is the paper's method itself reproducible, not just its conclusions?
basis: Our replication explicitly labels C7 (the paper-specific pipeline: 2690-locus schema + k-mer binning + digital DNA-tiling-array SARA/SARB mining) as not-rerun because the custom schema and legacy array data are not redistributable as drop-in artifacts. We claim the conclusions were replicated, not the method. A stronger scientific test is whether an independent researcher can reconstruct an equivalent schema (open-source: chewBBACA on the same 150 complete-genome seed set) and get the same lineage assignments.
next_steps: Download the same 150 complete Salmonella genome seed set that the paper used (from NCBI Assembly, using the paper's Supplementary Table); run chewBBACA CreateSchema then AlleleCall on the 82 Bovismorbificans genomes to derive an independent 2500-3000-locus core schema; compare the resulting cgMLST distance matrix to our mash matrix (Mantel test) and to a re-implemented k-mer-binning distance (e.g. sourmash gather at k=31,51); publish the reconstructed schema as an open resource; ask whether the SARA/SARB tiling-array signal can be replaced with a modern in-silico probe approach (e.g. BLAST of the array probe sequences, if the paper's supplement lists them, against modern Salmonella assemblies).
